questions.question: Which of the following is the best example of a carnivore?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Lion**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A **carnivore** is a biological organism that primarily derives its energy and nutrient requirements from a diet consisting of **animal tissue**, whether through predation or scavenging.
 
• The **Lion** (Panthera leo) is a quintessential example of an **obligate carnivore**, meaning its biological system is physically adapted to require nutrients found only in animal flesh.
 
• Lions function as **apex predators** in their ecosystems, predominantly the **African savannas** and the Gir Forest in India, where they regulate the populations of large ungulates.
 
• Scientific studies of their anatomy reveal specialized **carnassial teeth** and powerful jaws designed for shearing meat, alongside a relatively **short digestive tract** optimized for rapid protein absorption.
 
• In the **trophic level** hierarchy, lions occupy the position of **secondary or tertiary consumers**, playing a vital role in maintaining the **ecological balance** of their habitats.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Dietary Classifications of Other Options**:

 
 
• **Herbivores**: Organisms like the **Cow** feed exclusively on plants. They possess complex **ruminant stomachs** and flat teeth designed for grinding **cellulose**.
 
• **Omnivores**: Animals like the **Crow** have a diverse diet including both plant matter (seeds, fruits) and animal matter (insects, small rodents), allowing them to adapt to various **biomes**.
 
• **Parasites**: The **Tapeworm** is an endoparasite that lives within the **intestines** of a host. Unlike carnivores that hunt and consume prey, parasites absorb **pre-digested nutrients** directly from the host organism.
 
 
 
• **Ecological Importance**:
 
 
• Carnivores prevent **overgrazing** by controlling the density of **primary consumers**, which in turn protects the **vegetation cover** and biodiversity of the region.

questions.question: The splitting of white light into colors was first explained by:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Isaac Newton**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In **1666**, the English scientist **Sir Isaac Newton** performed a landmark experiment using a **glass prism** to investigate the nature of light.
 
• He observed that when a narrow beam of sunlight (white light) passed through the prism, it spread out into a multi-colored band called a **spectrum**.
 
• This phenomenon is known as **dispersion**, which occurs because white light is a mixture of different colors that travel at different speeds through the glass.
 
• Newton identified the seven constituent colors as **Red**, **Orange**, **Yellow**, **Green**, **Blue**, **Indigo**, and **Violet**, often abbreviated as **VIBGYOR**.
 
• He proved that the prism was not coloring the light by using a **second inverted prism** to recombine the colored rays back into a single beam of **white light**.
 
• The experiment concluded that **refraction** depends on the wavelength; **violet light** has a shorter wavelength and bends the most, while **red light** has a longer wavelength and bends the least.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Thomas Young**:

 
 
• Famous for the **Double-Slit Experiment** conducted in **1801**.
 
• He demonstrated the **interference** of light, which provided critical evidence for the **wave theory of light**.
 
 
 
• **Christiaan Huygens**:
 
 
• A Dutch physicist who proposed the **wave theory of light** in **1678**.
 
• He developed the **Huygens-Fresnel principle**, explaining how **wavefronts** propagate through space.
 
 
 
• **James Clerk Maxwell**:
 
 
• Formulated the **Maxwell equations** in the **1860s**, unifying electricity and magnetism.
 
• He mathematically proved that light is an **electromagnetic wave** that travels at the speed of light.

questions.question: By how much was the Indian rupee devalued in July 1991 to tackle the balance of payments crisis?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**18-20%**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In **July 1991**, India faced a severe **Balance of Payments (BoP) crisis**, where foreign exchange reserves had dropped to approximately 1.2 billion dollars, barely enough to sustain two weeks of essential imports.
 
• The **Reserve Bank of India (RBI)** intervened by devaluing the **Indian Rupee** in two sharp steps to restore economic stability and international confidence.
 
• The first downward adjustment occurred on **July 1, 1991**, when the value of the rupee was reduced by about **9%** against major international currencies.
 
• The second adjustment followed quickly on **July 3, 1991**, with a further devaluation of about **11%**, bringing the cumulative devaluation to the range of **18-20%**.
 
• The primary objective of this **exchange rate adjustment** was to make **Indian exports** cheaper and more competitive globally while making **imports** more expensive to curb the widening trade deficit.
 
• This measure was a critical component of the structural adjustment program required to secure emergency assistance from the **International Monetary Fund (IMF)** and the **World Bank**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Balance of Payments (BoP) Crisis of 1991**:

 
 
• The crisis was exacerbated by the **Gulf War (1990-91)**, which caused a spike in **crude oil prices** and reduced inward **remittances** from the Middle East.
 
• High **fiscal deficits** and **external debt** throughout the 1980s had made the Indian economy vulnerable to external shocks.
 
 
 
• **New Economic Policy (NEP)**:
 
 
• The devaluation acted as a catalyst for the **Liberalization, Privatization, and Globalization (LPG)** reforms introduced under the leadership of Prime Minister **P.V. Narasimha Rao** and Finance Minister **Dr. Manmohan Singh**.
 
• These reforms dismantled the **License Raj**, reduced **import tariffs**, and opened the Indian economy to **Foreign Direct Investment (FDI)**.
 
 
 
• **Evolution of Exchange Rate System**:
 
 
• Following the 1991 crisis, India moved from a **fixed exchange rate** regime to a **Liberalized Exchange Rate Management System (LERMS)** in 1992, and eventually to a **managed float system** where market forces largely determine the rupee's value.

• Its primary mandate is to provide financial assistance to Indian exporters and importers while promoting **foreign trade** through various innovative credit programs.

• A **flow variable** is an economic quantity that is measured over a **specific period of time**, such as a month, a quarter, or a **fiscal year**.
 
• **National income** represents the total value of all final goods and services produced by the normal residents of a country during an **accounting year** (usually from April 1 to March 31 in India).
 
• It is categorized as a flow because it reflects the **continuous generation** of value, wages, interest, and profits over a time interval rather than a static amount held at one moment.
 
• The measurement of **National income** involves calculating the **Net National Product at Factor Cost** (NNP at FC), which requires aggregating economic activities throughout the year.

• **Foreign Exchange Reserves**: These are the **foreign assets**, gold, and **Special Drawing Rights** (SDRs) held by the **Reserve Bank of India** (RBI) at a specific point in time to maintain **liquidity** and stability in the currency market.

• Under this law, a **District Magistrate** was empowered to call upon the printer and publisher of any vernacular newspaper to enter into a bond undertaking not to cause disaffection against the government.

__
 
• **Water storage in ice and snow** refers to the accumulation of frozen freshwater in **glaciers**, **ice caps**, and permanent snowfields. **Evapotranspiration** is the collective process of **evaporation** from surfaces and **transpiration** from plants, primarily involving liquid water and biological activity. The direct transition of ice or snow into water vapor is known as **sublimation**, not evapotranspiration. ***Hence, statement I is incorrect.***
 
• **Groundwater storage** constitutes the water located beneath the Earth's surface in soil pore spaces and the fractures of rock formations, known as **aquifers**. **Groundwater discharge** occurs when this subsurface water moves toward the surface; **springs** are the natural locations where this stored water flows out onto the land or into water bodies. ***Hence, statement II is correct.***

• **Hydrological Cycle Components**:

 
 
• **Sublimation**: This process allows **ice and snow** to enter the atmosphere as vapor without melting into liquid water first. It is a critical factor in the mass balance of **glaciers**.
 
• **Transpiration**: The process by which moisture is carried through plants from roots to small pores on the underside of leaves, where it changes to vapor and is released to the atmosphere.
 
• **Aquifers**: These are permeable layers of **sediment** or **rock** that act as underground reservoirs. They are replenished through **infiltration** and **percolation**.
 
• **Water Table**: The upper surface of the **zone of saturation**, where the pressure of groundwater is equal to atmospheric pressure. When the water table meets the land surface, a **spring** or **wetland** is formed.

questions.question: What is the smallest number that is a multiple of 7, 10, 14 and 20?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

To find the **smallest number** that is a multiple of 7, 10, 14, and 20, identify the **Least Common Multiple (LCM)**.

Pick the **largest number** (20) and check its multiples: 20, 40, 60, 80, 100, 120, 140...

Check **divisibility** for each: 140 is the first multiple divisible by both **7** and **14**.

Since 140 is also divisible by 10, it is the **smallest common multiple**.

**∴ The correct answer is 140.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Numbers are 7, 10, 14, and 20.

**Formula Used:** **LCM** = Product of the **highest powers** of all prime factors involved.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/5c704fe1faf00eb164a75fe2a93578e7ac3232cb6cc19019801a4cfe5f7ae0ae.png] 

⇒ **Prime factorization** of numbers:

⇒ 7 = 7¹

⇒ 10 = 2¹ × 5¹

⇒ 14 = 2¹ × 7¹

⇒ 20 = 2² × 5¹

⇒ LCM = 2² × 5¹ × 7¹

⇒ LCM = 4 × 5 × 7 = 140

**∴ The correct answer is 140.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Least Common Multiple (LCM)

The **LCM** of a set of numbers is the smallest integer that is exactly divisible by every number in that set.

Highest Common Factor (HCF)

The **HCF** is the greatest number that divides two or more numbers without leaving a remainder.

Fundamental Property of LCM and HCF

For any two numbers **a** and **b**, the product of the numbers is equal to the product of their **HCF** and **LCM** (a × b = HCF × LCM).

questions.question: When 10 percent of a number is added to 15 percent of the same number, then the result is 3375. What is the value of the number?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Combine the **percentages** directly since they apply to the same **number**: 10% + 15% = 25%.

As per the given condition, 25% of the **number** → 3375.

We know that 25% is equivalent to the **fraction** 1/4.

Total **number** (100%) = 3375 × 4 = 13500.

**∴ The correct answer is 13500.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Sum of 10% and 15% of a **number** is 3375.

**Formula Used:** Value = (Percentage ÷ 100) × **Original Number**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/8c406197e98fa6c6d7f9a819befe07ddcbe5c9fc8b4381e614e0f175ec49dfd0.png] 

⇒ Let the **number** be x.

⇒ 10% of x + 15% of x = 3375

⇒ (10 ÷ 100) × x + (15 ÷ 100) × x = 3375

⇒ 0.10x + 0.15x = 3375

⇒ 0.25x = 3375

⇒ x = 3375 ÷ 0.25

⇒ x = (3375 × 100) ÷ 25

⇒ x = 3375 × 4

⇒ x = 13500

**∴ The correct answer is 13500.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Percentage Addition Rule

If multiple **percentages** are calculated on the same **base value**, they can be added or subtracted directly before performing the multiplication: a% of x + b% of x = (a + b)% of x.

Common Fraction Conversions

Converting percentages to **fractions** simplifies calculations: 25% = 1/4, 20% = 1/5, 10% = 1/10, and 50% = 1/2.

Finding the Original Value

To find the 100% value (the **number** itself) when a certain percentage P% is known as value V: Original Number = (V ÷ P) × 100.

questions.question: Selling price of an article is Rs. 510. Loss percentage is 15 percent. What is the cost price of the article?

[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Convert **Loss percentage** to fraction: 15% = 3/20.

If **Cost Price (CP)** = 20 units, then **Loss** = 3 units.

**Selling Price (SP)** = CP − Loss = 20 − 3 = 17 units.

Given 17 units = **₹510** ⇒ 1 unit = 510 ÷ 17 = **₹30**.

**Cost Price** = 20 units = 20 × 30 = **₹600**.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹600.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**Selling price** (SP) = ₹510

**Loss percentage** (L%) = 15%

**Formula Used:**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/881b4287e76076f547ddf7486cba28270725be1a669b2fa7857b62c1adcdee09.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ CP = [100 ÷ (100 − 15)] × 510

⇒ CP = [100 ÷ 85] × 510

⇒ CP = [20 ÷ 17] × 510

⇒ CP = 20 × 30

⇒ CP = ₹600

**∴ The correct answer is ₹600.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Profit and Loss Percentage

Profit % = (Profit ÷ CP) × 100, where Profit = SP − CP. Loss % = (Loss ÷ CP) × 100, where Loss = CP − SP.

Marked Price and Discount

Discount is always offered on the **Marked Price (MP)**. SP = MP × (100 − Discount%) ÷ 100.

Successive Discounts

For two successive discounts of a% and b%, the effective single discount is (a + b − ab ÷ 100)%.

questions.question: Weight of A and B are in the ratio of 6 : 5. B's weight increases by 20 percent. Total weight of A and B increases by 40 percent. If total weight of them becomes 154 kg, then what is the weight of A after the increment?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Let the **Initial Weights** be 60 kg and 50 kg (Ratio 6 : 5) ⇒ **Total Initial Weight** = 110 kg.

**New Total Weight** (40% increase) = 110 × 1.4 = 154 kg. (Matches given data).

**New Weight of B** (20% increase) = 50 × 1.2 = 60 kg.

**Weight of A after increment** = **New Total** − **New B** = 154 − 60 = 94 kg.

**∴ The correct answer is 94 kg.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**Ratio of weights of A and B** = 6 : 5

**Increase in B** = 20%

**Increase in Total Weight** = 40%

**Final Total Weight** = 154 kg

**Formula Used:**

**Final Value** = **Initial Value** × (1 + **Percentage Increase** ÷ 100)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/911a4b831015331ca6f10405b16c820aac1ff2628db560fb646f665cdc2332b4.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ **Initial Total Weight** = 154 ÷ 1.4 = 110 kg

⇒ **Sum of Ratio Parts** = 6 + 5 = 11 units

⇒ **Initial Weight of A** = (6 ÷ 11) × 110 = 60 kg

⇒ **Initial Weight of B** = (5 ÷ 11) × 110 = 50 kg

⇒ **Weight of B after 20% increase** = 50 + (20% of 50) = 50 + 10 = 60 kg

⇒ **Weight of A after increment** = **New Total Weight** − **New Weight of B**

⇒ **Weight of A after increment** = 154 − 60 = 94 kg

**∴ The correct answer is 94 kg.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Weighted Average in Percentages

Percentage Multiplier Method

To increase a value by x%, multiply the original value by (1 + x/100). To decrease, multiply by (1 − x/100).

questions.question: A pipe can fill 5/6 part of a tank in 60 minutes. What part of the same tank it can fill in 30 minutes?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The **part filled** is **directly proportional** to the **time** elapsed when the **filling rate** is constant.

Given: **60 minutes** → **5/6 part**

Since **30 minutes** is exactly **half** of 60 minutes, the part filled will also be **half**.

New Part = (5/6) × (30/60) = (5/6) × (1/2) = 5/12.

**∴ The correct answer is 5/12 part.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Part of tank filled (P₁) = 5/6

Time taken (T₁) = 60 min

Target Time (T₂) = 30 min

**Formula Used:**

**Rate** of filling = **Part filled** ÷ **Time taken**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3daaa31f080a78c9cd3b27ec57878c0c9d60d1aaf4160fa7519c11d343261184.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Rate of filling = (5/6) ÷ 60

⇒ Rate = 5 / (6 × 60) = 5/360 = 1/72 part per minute

⇒ Part filled in 30 minutes = Rate × Time

⇒ Part filled = (1/72) × 30

⇒ Part filled = 30/72

⇒ Dividing numerator and denominator by 6:

⇒ Part filled = 5/12

**∴ The correct answer is 5/12 part.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Direct Variation

In filling problems, the **quantity** (part of the tank) is **directly proportional** to **time** (Q ∝ T), provided the rate of the pipe remains constant.

Filling Rate Formula

If a pipe fills a tank in **'x' minutes**, its filling rate is **1/x part** of the tank per minute.

Combined Pipes Rule

If pipe A fills a tank in **'a'** time and pipe B fills it in **'b'** time, together they fill **(1/a + 1/b) part** in unit time.

questions.question: A train of length 300 metres crosses a another train of length 500 metres in 90 seconds. They are travelling in opposite directions. If the speed of both the trains is same, then what is the speed (in km/hr) of each train?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total distance to cover = Sum of **train lengths** = 300 + 500 = 800 m.

In **opposite directions**, relative speed = S₁ + S₂ = 2 × Speed (as speeds are same).

Relative Speed = Distance ÷ Time = 800 ÷ 90 = 80/9 m/s.

Speed of each train = (1/2) × (80/9) × (18/5) km/hr = 16 km/hr.

**∴ The correct answer is 16 km/hr.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Length of first train (L₁) = 300 m, Length of second train (L₂) = 500 m, **Time** (T) = 90 sec, Speed of both trains is equal (v).

**Formula:** Relative Speed = (L₁ + L₂) ÷ T

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3b1ee5cf6634798224e7816d79f73db2a6d3efddd41d718e917f3b3638c46286.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total Distance = 300 + 500 = 800 m

⇒ Relative Speed (v + v) = 800 ÷ 90

⇒ 2v = 80/9 m/s

⇒ v = 40/9 m/s

⇒ To convert **m/s to km/hr**, multiply by 18/5:

⇒ Speed (v) = (40 ÷ 9) × (18 ÷ 5)

⇒ v = 8 × 2 = 16 km/hr

**∴ The correct answer is 16 km/hr.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Relative Speed in Opposite Directions

When two objects move towards each other, their **relative speed** is the sum of their individual speeds: Vᵣₑₗ = V₁ + V₂.

Unit Conversion

To convert speed from **m/s to km/hr**, multiply by 18/5. To convert from **km/hr to m/s**, multiply by 5/18.

Crossing Objects with Length

When a train crosses another train or a bridge, the **total distance** covered is the sum of the lengths of both objects.

questions.question: The marked price of an article is 30 percent more than its cost price. If the profit earned is 10 percent, then what is the discount offered on the article?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Let **Cost Price (CP)** be 100 units.

**Marked Price (MP)** = 100 + 30% of 100 = 130 units.

**Selling Price (SP)** = 100 + 10% **Profit** = 110 units.

**Discount** offered = **MP** − **SP** = 130 − 110 = 20 units.

**Discount %** = (20 ÷ 130) × 100 = 200/13 %.

**∴ The correct answer is (200/13) percent.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**Markup Percentage** = 30%

**Profit Percentage** = 10%

**Formula Used:**

1. **Selling Price (SP)** = **Cost Price (CP)** + **Profit**

2. **Discount** = **Marked Price (MP)** − **Selling Price (SP)**

3. **Discount %** = (**Discount** ÷ **MP**) × 100

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/43df79894d0e9599872b318a3e426f2ab8227072cfeb14a0250390903aeb4671.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the **Cost Price (CP)** of the article be 100.

⇒ **Marked Price (MP)** = 100 + (30% of 100) = 130.

⇒ **Selling Price (SP)** = 100 + (10% profit of 100) = 110.

⇒ **Discount Amount** = **MP** − **SP** = 130 − 110 = 20.

⇒ **Discount Percentage** = (**Discount Amount** ÷ **Marked Price**) × 100.

⇒ **Discount Percentage** = (20 ÷ 130) × 100 = 200/13 %.

**∴ The correct answer is (200/13) percent.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Relationship between CP, MP, Profit and Discount

The direct ratio formula is: MP ÷ CP = (100 + Profit %) ÷ (100 − Discount %). This is very useful when any three values are known.

Successive Percentage Method

Profit % = Markup % − Discount % − (Markup % × Discount %) ÷ 100. This treats the markup and discount as successive changes to the CP.

Markup Definition

Markup is the extra price added to the **Cost Price** to reach the **Marked Price**, expressed as Markup % = ((MP − CP) ÷ CP) × 100.

questions.question: 3.6, 1.2, x and 15 are in proportion. What is the value of x?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Ratio of the first two terms = 3.6 : 1.2 = **3 : 1**.

Since the numbers are in **proportion**, the ratio of the last two terms must also be **3 : 1**.

x : 15 = 3 : 1 ⇒ x = 15 × 3 = 45.

**∴ The correct answer is 45.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** 3.6, 1.2, x, and 15 are in **proportion**.

**Formula Used:** If a, b, c, and d are in proportion, then a ÷ b = c ÷ d (or Product of Extremes = Product of Means).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/5d0976118c2da09e22ffb0c5636abee8810c2dfdda7337566306343f912295be.png] 

According to the **proportionality rule**:

⇒ 3.6 ÷ 1.2 = x ÷ 15

⇒ 3 = x ÷ 15

⇒ x = 3 × 15

⇒ x = 45

**∴ The correct answer is 45.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Basic Proportion Rule

Four numbers a, b, c, d are in **proportion** if a : b = c : d, which implies ad = bc.

Mean Proportional

The **mean proportional** between two numbers a and b is given by √(a × b).

Third Proportional

If a, b, and c are in **continued proportion** (a : b = b : c), then the third proportional c = b² ÷ a.

Fourth Proportional

In the proportion a : b = c : d, d is called the **fourth proportional** and is calculated as (b × c) ÷ a.

Which of the following options is the most suitable conversion of the following sentence into Passive Voice?
The company will release the new product next week.

options.text: The new product will be released by the company next week.
The new product is going to release by the company next week.
The new product will have been released by the company next week.
The new product was released by the company next week.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**The new product will be released by the company next week**__.

**__Key Points__**

__

• The given sentence is in the **Active Voice** and the **Simple Future Tense**. The structure of the active sentence is: **Subject (The company) + will + V1 (release) + Object (the new product) + Time Reference (next week)**.

• To convert a sentence from active to passive voice in the **Simple Future Tense**, the object of the active sentence becomes the subject of the passive sentence. The auxiliary verb **will** is followed by **be** and the **Past Participle (V3)** form of the main verb.

• The **Past Participle** of the verb **release** is **released**. Thus, the construction becomes: **The new product + will + be + released**.

• In the passive voice, the **agent** (the original subject) is usually introduced by the preposition **by**. Therefore, **by the company** is added after the verb phrase.

• Combining these elements, the correct passive structure is: **The new product will be released by the company next week**.

 **Additional Information__**

• **Voice Transformation Rules**:

• **Future Perfect Tense**: If the active sentence was in the **Future Perfect** (e.g., will have released), the passive form would use **will have been released**. This is why option 3 is incorrect for the given sentence.

• **Simple Past Tense**: The passive structure **was released** is reserved for the **Simple Past Tense** (e.g., The company released the product). Since the original sentence uses **will**, option 4 is grammatically mismatched in terms of tense.

• **Going to form**: While **is going to** indicates future intent, the phrasing **is going to release** in option 2 is still in the active voice and lacks the **be + V3** structure required for a passive construction.

• **Subject-Object Swap**: The primary function of the passive voice is to shift the **focus** from the performer of the action (The company) to the receiver of the action (The new product).

</ul

**__Key Points__**

• The original sentence contains a **double negative** error. The word **Unless** is a **subordinating conjunction** that means **if... not** or **except if**.
 
• Since **Unless** already carries a negative meaning, it should not be followed by another negative word like **not** in the same clause. Doing so creates a logical contradiction that fails to convey the intended condition.
 
• To correct this, we can either remove the word **not** (e.g., **Unless traffic rules are made...**) or replace **Unless** with **If** while keeping the negative **not**.
 
• The option **If traffic rules are not made more stringent** correctly establishes the **conditional clause**. It indicates that the failure to make rules stricter will result in the continuation of accidents.
 
• The structure **If + subject + negative verb** is a standard way to express a negative condition in English grammar, making it the most suitable replacement for the underlined part.

 **Additional Information__**

 
• **Understanding Conjunctions:**
 
 
• **Unless**: Used to express a **negative condition**. It is followed by an **affirmative verb**. Example: **Unless you work hard, you will not succeed**.
 
• **If... not**: This is the functional equivalent of **unless**. Example: **If you do not work hard, you will not succeed**.
 
• **Until/Till**: These are **temporal conjunctions** used to refer to a **point in time** or the duration of an action. They mean **up to the time that**. Using them in this context is incorrect because the sentence requires a **condition**, not a **time limit**.
